text:
Twelve-year-old Sunita used to stare blankly at her tattered slate, her attendance slipping as chores and lost lessons piled up. Living in the remote terrain of Jhabua district, Madhya Pradesh, school felt like a distant luxury until Asha Society stepped in. Set up in 2006, our organisation witnessed firsthand how adolescent girls drop out when academic gaps widen.

Today, we are launching an 11-month initiative with a total budget of Rs 12,60,000 to transform educational realities for 3,120 adolescent girls. Our primary goal is to raise the attendance rate from 70% to 77% by directly addressing the root causes of absenteeism.

The project activities are carefully tailored to keep these young learners engaged and in school. We are turning traditional classrooms into vibrant digital learning spaces equipped with tablets, making education interactive and modern. Furthermore, we are providing small scholarship grants so girls can stay enrolled without financial anxiety, alongside after-school remedial classes for children who have fallen behind.

To ensure every rupee of the CSR funding is utilised effectively, our financial allocation is structured across three key cost heads: learning materials account for Rs 9,02,000; infrastructure upgrades require Rs 2,63,000; and administration and monitoring is set at Rs 95,000. Through this holistic approach, girls like Sunita will no longer slip through the cracks, securing a brighter, educated future for their community.

Technical Proposal for CSR Grant Assistance

Applicant Organisation: Jal Sansthan, operational since 1993.
Target Location: Sahibganj district, Jharkhand.
Total Grant Requested: Rs 55,00,000.
Project Duration: 14 months.
Target Beneficiaries: 4,460 village residents.

Project Overview and Technical Approach:
Jal Sansthan proposes a comprehensive healthcare initiative aimed at raising antenatal coverage from 42% to 66% in Sahibganj district, Jharkhand, over a period of 14 months. The project targets 4,460 village residents through a structured mix of preventive and curative community health services.

The field operations comprise several core activities. A qualified doctor and nurse will conduct regular health camps in every target village. Concurrently, the project team will organise community vaccination drives executed in coordination with the local health centre. Additionally, specialised screening sessions will be held for women and adolescents to detect anaemia, accompanied by the distribution of iron supplements.

- Procurement of diagnostic equipment: Rs 32,87,000
- Execution of mobile camp operations: Rs 8,74,000
- Procurement of essential medical supplies: Rs 7,34,000

Progress will be tracked through weekly field reports submitted by the attending doctors and nurses, logging patient attendance, screening counts, and supplement distribution volumes. Monthly review meetings will be convened with the local health centre to reconcile vaccination records against target milestones. Furthermore, baseline and endline household surveys will be administered among the 4,460 village residents to quantify changes in antenatal registration rates. Financial tracking will employ double-entry accounting software, with quarterly expenditure audits mapped against the sanctioned budgets for diagnostic equipment (Rs 32,87,000), mobile camps (Rs 8,74,000), and medical supplies (Rs 7,34,000). This rigorous tracking mechanism guarantees that corrective actions are taken promptly to achieve project objectives within the 14-month timeframe.

We are seeking a total funding requested amount of Rs 10,20,000 for implementing a vital community development project located in Barmer district, Rajasthan. Secondly, we will construct new school toilets equipped with running water infrastructure. Through the synchronized execution of daily hot meals and improved sanitation amenities over the 9 months timeline, we are fully confident of successfully raising the attendance rate from 60% to 68% for the 1,540 primary school children. Gramin Foundation brings years of grassroots experience since 1990 to ensure proper implementation, day-to-day management, and transparent reporting of all activities undertaken in Barmer district, Rajasthan. 

We sincerely hope your esteemed corporation will kindly sanction our funding requested sum of Rs 10,20,000 under your corporate social responsibility initiatives. Thank you very much for your valuable time and consideration.

Yours faithfully,
Gramin Foundation

Dear Friends and Partners in Corporate Social Responsibility,

At Gramin Samiti, working since 1994, our hearts ache when we see young minds slipping through the cracks of a fragile educational system. Education is the singular ladder out of generational poverty, yet foundational learning gaps keep holding our children back. Our overarching goal is to raise average daily attendance from 68% to 77%, ensuring that children are not only present in classrooms but are actively engaged. To accomplish this, we will implement remedial sessions in reading and arithmetic, conduct workshops that train government teachers in activity-based teaching, and construct new school toilets with running water to secure dignity and hygiene, particularly for growing girls.

To bring this vision to life, we request funding requested of Rs 16,10,000. Partner with Gramin Samiti under Section 135 to give these children the future they deserve.

With gratitude,
Founder, Gramin Samiti

text:
Subject: CSR Proposal for Women's Economic Empowerment and Livelihoods in Barwani

Dear CSR Team,

Greetings from Arogya Collective! Established in 2019, our organisation has been consistently working on grassroots livelihood interventions in Madhya Pradesh. We are writing to seek your valuable partnership for our upcoming initiative in Barwani district, Madhya Pradesh, spanning 22 months.

Rural women face systemic barriers to entering the formal workforce. To address this, we propose an integrated project focusing on women in self-help groups. Our approach combines agricultural enhancement through drip irrigation kits for small farmers, skill-building via vocational courses in trades with local demand, and creative design workshops so artisans can make products buyers want. These synchronized interventions will tackle both agricultural productivity and non-farm income generation, aiming to raise women's participation in paid work from 18% to 27%.

To execute this comprehensive plan effectively, we request a total funding of Rs 37,10,000. Our transparent spending plan allocates Rs 8,52,000 for course fees, Rs 9,63,000 for market access, Rs 9,51,000 for working capital support, Rs 6,88,000 for equipment and inputs, and Rs 2,56,000 for overheads and monitoring.

Your support will directly transform the economic landscape for numerous households. We would be delighted to arrange a detailed discussion or share further documentation regarding this project at your earliest convenience.

Warm regards,

Director, Arogya Collective
style: a concise email to a company's CSR team

Subject: CSR Partnership Proposal for Agricultural Livelihood Enhancement in Jaisalmer

Dear CSR Team,

Greetings from Navjeevan Collective! Operating since 2000, we have dedicated ourselves to uplifting vulnerable agrarian communities in Rajasthan. We are reaching out to present a high-impact initiative aimed at transforming farming livelihoods in Jaisalmer district, Rajasthan, over a duration of 24 months.

Water scarcity and limited technical know-how severely constrain the income of smallholder farmers in the region. This project is specifically tailored to support 330 smallholder farmers. The planned intervention strategy encompasses helping smallholders switch to drip watering to conserve precious groundwater, alongside intensive skill training linked to apprenticeships to diversify their income streams. Through these concerted efforts, we target a tangible outcome: to raise monthly household earnings by 18%.

To achieve these goals, we require a total budget of Rs 10,80,000. Our judiciously designed spending plan is structured as follows: Rs 3,07,000 for tools and raw materials, Rs 6,87,000 for working capital, and Rs 86,000 for administration and monitoring. Every rupee will be prudently utilised to ensure maximum social return on investment.

We believe this partnership will create a lasting, positive footprint in the community. We welcome the opportunity to present our proposal in greater detail and discuss how your corporate values align with our mission.

Sincerely,

Project Coordinator, Navjeevan Collective

Project Title: Enhancing Educational Retention and Infrastructure in Sonbhadra

Applicant: Udyam Society (set up in 2005)
Project Area: Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh
Project Cost: Rs 13,10,000
Timeline: 13 months
Participants: 3,850 students in grades 6-8
Target Outcome: Raise attendance rate from 58% to 64%

Planned Work:
The initiative deploys small scholarship grants so girls can stay enrolled, complemented by infrastructure development involving building separate toilets for girls and boys at schools to improve sanitation and dignity.

Monitoring and Evaluation Framework:
Udyam Society will implement a rigorous monitoring mechanism to track progress throughout the 13 months. Field coordinators will conduct monthly audits of school attendance registers, verifying baseline and milestone data against the target outcome of raising the attendance rate from 58% to 64%. Infrastructure milestones for building separate toilets for girls and boys at schools will be supervised by our resident civil engineer, with photo-documentation submitted in quarterly review reports. Any variance from projected indicators will trigger immediate corrective action meetings with school management committees, ensuring full transparency and accountability for the Rs 13,10,000 project cost.

Eight months pregnant and battling severe exhaustion, Kamla from a remote hamlet in Jhabua district, Madhya Pradesh, had resigned herself to giving birth without ever seeing a doctor. Clinics were too far, and transport was a luxury her family could not afford.

Navjeevan Foundation, founded 2015, refuses to let expectant mothers face such risks. For 18 months, we are executing a vital maternal health project across Jhabua district, Madhya Pradesh, supporting pregnant women. Our model deploys regular health camps run by a doctor and nurse in each village, innovative telemedicine kiosks where villagers consult doctors by video, and catch-up immunisation sessions for children who missed vaccines.

This holistic healthcare delivery system aims to raise the share of pregnant women receiving antenatal care from 68% to 75%. We request a total budget of Rs 24,50,000 to implement these life-saving measures.

Eighteen-year-old Sonali sat on the porch of her modest home in Yavatmal district, Maharashtra, anxiously feeling her swollen abdomen. Five months pregnant and without transport, she had missed every local health check-up, terrified that complications would go unnoticed as they had for her neighbours.

Pragati Mission, working since 2016, refuses to let expectant mothers face such preventable dangers. Over a 24-month project period, we are rolling out a comprehensive maternal and child healthcare initiative across Yavatmal district, Maharashtra, dedicated to 5,400 pregnant women.

Our field operations combine regular antenatal check-ups for pregnant women, refresher courses for local health workers to upgrade their frontline clinical skills, and catch-up immunisation sessions for children who missed vaccines. By establishing reliable grassroots healthcare delivery, we aim to raise the share of pregnant women receiving antenatal care from 62% to 79%.

To execute this vital project, we are seeking a total budget of Rs 36,10,000. Our transparent spending plan allocates Rs 6,37,000 for diagnostic equipment, Rs 10,30,000 for running the health camps, Rs 16,71,000 for medicines and consumables, and Rs 2,72,000 for admin and reporting.

With your CSR partnership, we can ensure that no mother in Yavatmal is left without essential care during her most vulnerable months.

A Persuasive Appeal from the Founder

Dear Corporate Partners,

Since our inception in 1992, Seva Society has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the most vulnerable rural populations, striving to bridge critical gaps in basic services. Today, I write to you on behalf of Seva Society to urge your generous investment in our upcoming healthcare initiative located in Sahibganj district, Jharkhand.

In many remote hamlets across this region, preventable diseases continue to take a heavy toll simply because mothers and young children lack timely medical access. Pregnant women face immense vulnerabilities without adequate local support, and infants frequently miss life-saving inoculations during their crucial developmental months. To address this urgent crisis, we have designed a targeted 20-month intervention focused on lasting community change. Our overarching expected change is to raise full immunisation coverage among children to 69%.

To achieve this ambitious target, our team will deploy two core strategies. We will conduct rigorous vaccination drives run with the local health centre, ensuring vaccines reach the remotest doorsteps. Simultaneously, we will execute refresher courses for local health workers, sharpening their clinical skills, improving their tracking mechanisms, and empowering them to serve their communities with greater confidence and competence.

To bring this vital project to life, we are seeking a funding contribution of Rs 22,40,000 (22.4 lakh). Every rupee of this grant will be utilised prudently and transparently. Our detailed budget breakdown allocates Rs 10,03,000 for field staff stipends, Rs 10,04,000 for essential medical supplies, and Rs 2,33,000 for management costs.

Partnering with Seva Society under Section 135 is not merely a compliance obligation; it is a profound opportunity to save young lives and secure a healthier future for generations to come. We invite your CSR team to join hands with us in Sahibganj.

With deep gratitude and warm regards,
Founder, Seva Society

Arogya Trust, founded 2000, envisions transforming the lives of handloom weavers in this region. Over a project period of 22 months, our initiative aims to raise women in paid work to 28% across the district.

Our comprehensive activities include strengthening a village dairy cooperative with chilling equipment, connecting artisans to buyers through market linkage, and hosting design workshops so artisans can make products buyers want.

The total budget of Rs 29,00,000 is meticulously allocated to ensure maximum grassroots impact. Our spending plan covers working capital support Rs 15,78,000, equipment Rs 7,63,000, and overheads and monitoring Rs 5,59,000. Through this partnership under Section 135, we will revive traditional crafts and secure sustainable livelihoods.

text:
Dear CSR Partners,

I write to you today from Raichur district, Karnataka, on behalf of Prakriti Collective, registered in 2011. Our planet cries out for urgent ecological healing, and nowhere is this more apparent than in our degraded rural landscapes, where depleted green cover and pitch-black village lanes compound environmental and social vulnerabilities.

Over an 18-month project period, our dedicated team will work hand-in-hand with 5,000 community members to reverse this ecological decline. What will be done includes restoring degraded mangrove belts to protect coastal ecologies and installing solar-powered street lights in village lanes to ensure safe community movement after dusk. Through these synchronized interventions, our target outcome is to add 140 hectares of tree cover.

To achieve this ambitious vision, we require a total budget of Rs 32,30,000. Our transparent spending plan accounts for monitoring and maintenance Rs 14,60,000, saplings and materials Rs 8,48,000, project staff Rs 3,11,000, community engagement Rs 3,30,000, and admin and reporting Rs 2,81,000.

We invite your esteemed corporation to join hands with us under Section 135 of the Companies Act. Together, we can restore environmental vitality and uplift rural lives.

Warm regards,
Founder, Prakriti Collective

Organisation Profile
Sahyog Collective, registered in 2022, works closely with vulnerable agrarian communities to foster sustainable livelihoods and economic resilience.

Project Overview
Located in Goalpara district, Assam, this 17-month project is designed to directly support 1,340 smallholder farmers. The initiative focuses on helping smallholders switch to drip watering to conserve water and boost crop yields, alongside strengthening a village dairy cooperative with chilling equipment to prevent milk spoilage and improve market access.

The primary target outcome of this intervention is to raise monthly household earnings by 19%.

text:
Ramesh lives with his aging parents and two younger siblings in a remote village in Araria district, Bihar. For years, his family depended solely on an acre of unirrigated land, struggling through erratic monsoons that barely yielded enough crops to sustain them through the winter. Debt from local lenders mounted with every failed harvest, leaving Ramesh with few prospects. Stories like his are common across the region, which is why Sankalp Trust, set up in 2021, has stepped forward with a comprehensive livelihood intervention designed to break this cycle of rural poverty.

This project, spanning a project period of 14 months with a total budget of Rs 8,50,000 (8.5 lakh), directly targets 370 smallholder farmers like Ramesh. Our overarching goal is to raise family income by 32% through structured economic activities. To achieve this, what will be done includes dairy training and milk collection for cooperative members, product design training for artisans to enhance market appeal, and microcredit through self-help groups for small enterprises.

To ensure transparency and effective utilization of resources, the spending plan has been carefully allocated across essential cost heads: working capital support Rs 1,42,000; market linkage Rs 90,000; tools and raw materials Rs 2,19,000; training Rs 3,20,000; and administration and monitoring Rs 79,000. Through these concerted efforts, we envisage a sustainable transformation in the living standards of our participants, providing them with the necessary tools, skills, and financial backing to secure a prosperous future.
